topic: How does the hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balance efficiency and compactness in V-band satellite antenna designs?
consensus_response: The hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balances efficiency and compactness by mitigating transmission line loss per unit length due to increased array size. As the array dimension grows beyond 16x16, the SIW power divider is replaced by a hybrid SIW-waveguide power divider. This transition leads to a trade-off between good performance and compact configuration, affecting both performance and capacity. The high insertion loss of SIW arrays with larger dimensions (e.g., from 70% to 27.5%) implies that as array size increases, the overall system performance will be affected by reduced efficiency, potentially leading to capacity losses in satellite communication links.
reference_context: A wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid-integrated plate-array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links was presented, with a reflection coefficient bandwidth of 14.6% and a gain fluctuating less than 3 dB within the frequency band of 57-66 GHz.
